challenged_claim: A bounded two-dimensional marginal density together with a uniform conditional scalar density cap is enough, by itself, to bound an indefinite rank-three quadratic pushforward.
counterexample: For 0<delta<=1/2 let T be Uniform[-1/2,1/2], independent of Y with density one on the unit-area set in coordinates s=y1+y2,d=y1-y2 given by 1<=s<=exp(4/delta), -delta/(2s)<=d<=0. Then y1^2-y2^2 lies in [-delta/2,0], but P(|T^2+y1^2-y2^2|<=delta/2)>=sqrt(2delta), forcing any density cap to be at least sqrt(2/delta).
reason_target_not_refuted: The constructed Y is an arbitrary dependent two-dimensional law and is not shown to be an orthogonal projection of an original independent cap-one product source.
next_implication: QFORM-HIGH-ROW-PRODUCT-TRACE-v1 must retain full orthogonal-product-projection provenance rather than only the two cap inequalities.
